A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KVzip research. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark comparisons, latency and memory measurements, ablations, attention analyses and a behavioral case study.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds prompt-sensitivity and attention-source analyses in Appendix C.2. The separately attributed KVPress results are unnecessary to establish this assessment.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same reconstruction-based importance scoring, chunking and pair/head eviction procedures. The softmax-free variant already appears in v1. Prompt modifications in v2 are ablation controls; the proposed default algorithm remains unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds a standalone RULER aggregate in Appendix D, Figure 17, but v1 already evaluates RULER-derived tasks through SCBench. The new aggregate does not specify its constituent tasks or context conditions, preventing reliable determination of additional represented data or task coverage. The explicitly described original datasets remain.

E2.justification: The added RULER comparison jointly evaluates KVzip against DuoAttention, SnapKV and PyramidKV. In v1, DuoAttention appears in the separate head-level comparison, while standard benchmark plots compare against H2O, SnapKV and PyramidKV. Those original comparisons remain intact.

E3.justification: Added settings include original/paraphrased/omitted-prompt controls on SQuAD with Qwen2.5-7B at a 30% cache ratio, an attention diagnostic using a 2K-token NIAH context, and the reported Qwen3-8B RULER evaluation. The established benchmark protocols are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.2 tests sensitivity to repeat-prompt wording and omission, and measures whether maximum attention originates from the instruction or repeated context. Existing reconstruction, chunk-size, softmax-free, head-budget and privacy analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance-testing procedures. The added accuracies and attention-source proportions do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: New Table 2 reports SQuAD accuracies of 94.37%, 94.45% and 94.25% for original, paraphrased and omitted prompts, with SnapKV at 32.15%. Appendix C.2 adds repeated-context attention-source proportions of 98.1% overall and 99.4% among retained pairs. Figure 17 adds RULER curves showing near-full-cache performance at a 0.25 cache ratio. Existing result curves remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, Equations (1)–(2), chunking complexity derivation and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. The new acknowledgment that information-loss guarantees are absent adds a limitation, not a theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The principal claims remain reusable query-agnostic compression, 3–4× cache reduction, approximately 2× attention-latency improvement, and compatibility with quantization and head-level eviction. Replacing parameter-specific model names with family names in the abstract does not change these contributions.

C2.justification: New Appendix B explicitly acknowledges the absence of guarantees concerning compression-induced information loss. Appendix C.2 explains prompt insensitivity through the prompt's short length and attention dominated by repeated context. The privacy observation and compression-overhead tradeoff largely reiterate existing discussion.

D1.justification: v2 makes the Qwen2.5-7B/14B model labels explicit as the -1M variants, identifies FlashAttention-2 in Figure 8, supplies exact prompt-control inputs and documents the KVPress results source. Core pseudocode, hardware, baseline hyperparameters and the KVzip repository disclosure remain unchanged; the label clarifications do not establish reruns.

R1.justification: Section 5 and the references add Finch, Beyond RAG and InfiniPot. The discussion now acknowledges Corallo et al.'s concurrent query-agnostic compression for retrieval-augmented generation, refining the positioning without substantially rewriting related work. These citations do not establish additional evaluated baselines.

P1.justification: The main narrative is largely retained, with limited abstract, introduction and caption edits. v2 adds limitations and repeat-prompt subsections, expands Appendix D with subheadings and a RULER paragraph, reorganizes supplementary material, and updates contact, conference and funding text.

P2.justification: v2 adds the prompt-ablation table and RULER plot. The original prompt-example Tables 2–3 move to the end as Tables 3–4, and the head-score visualization moves from Figure 14 to Figure 24. Other changes involve captions, model labels and local placement; existing graphics and result curves are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix C.2 adds a useful check of previously untested prompt-wording and omission sensitivity, supported by an attention diagnostic. Explicit limitations and acknowledgment of concurrent query-agnostic work improve transparency. The original method and evidence remain intact. The added RULER plot has limited protocol detail, so it provides modest additional support rather than resolving a major evidential gap.
